title: Director of Innovation

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: With 90 years in vinyl graphic films and active presence at ISA and FESPA trade shows, Avery Dennison's Innovation Director is tasked with identifying next-generation technologies that maintain market leadership as the industry shifts toward longer-life, lower-maintenance solutions. Tedlar's 60+ years of proven PVF chemistry and -70°F to 230°F operating range addresses emerging customer demands in extreme-climate architectural projects and transit interiors where current cast vinyl technology reaches performance limits. This role personally owns: (1) scouting external IP and material science breakthroughs that can leapfrog competitive offerings, (2) validating new substrate technologies that reduce total cost of ownership for end customers (fewer replacements = stronger customer retention), (3) building innovation pipeline for sustainability-focused clients seeking ultra-durable alternatives to frequent vinyl replacement cycles. The innovation case is compelling: integrating Tedlar as a protective top layer would allow Avery Dennison to offer a 'Platinum Series' with documented 20-year outdoor warranties, opening new revenue in municipal transit contracts, architectural facade systems, and premium fleet graphics where durability specifications exceed current product capabilities.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: As Director of Innovation, [Name] scouts and evaluates emerging technologies and material science breakthroughs that could extend Avery Dennison's competitive advantage in the graphics and wrapping film market. This role has authority to initiate technology partnerships, licensing discussions, and co-development opportunities. They report to senior R&D or product leadership and collaborate cross-functionally with Product Development, Marketing, and Technical teams to build the innovation pipeline. Their scope spans identifying solutions that address performance gaps in current offerings—particularly in extreme-climate applications, ultra-durable architectural systems, and premium transit segments where specifications exceed existing cast vinyl capabilities.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Given Avery Dennison's current product portfolio (5-12 year outdoor life for wrapping films) and massive fleet projects like the 30,000-vehicle DPD wrap, the most relevant Tedlar use cases for [Name] are: (1) **Vehicle wraps and fleet graphics**: Tedlar as a protective overlaminate layer could extend Avery Dennison's Supreme Wrapping Film lifespan to 20+ years while adding graffiti resistance—critical for high-visibility municipal and corporate fleets. (2) **Architectural graphics and building wraps**: Tedlar's extreme temperature range (-70°F to 230°F) and zero-yellowing properties address performance limits in facade systems and outdoor architectural applications where current vinyl solutions fall short of emerging 15-20 year warranty requirements. (3) **Transit and rail interiors**: Tedlar's mold/mildew resistance and cleanability align with transit authority specifications that demand low-maintenance, vandal-resistant interior surfaces. These use cases directly enable Avery Dennison to create a differentiated premium tier that captures ultra-durable market segments currently inaccessible with existing technology.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: [Name] is measured on the commercial viability of technologies brought into the innovation pipeline—meaning solutions must deliver measurable performance advantages that translate to new revenue streams or market share gains. Key pain points they personally own include: (1) maintaining Avery Dennison's market leadership position against 3M and other competitors as customer demands shift toward longer-life, lower-maintenance solutions, (2) addressing end-customer complaints about premature fading, cracking, and UV degradation that erode brand reputation and trigger warranty claims, (3) identifying technologies that reduce total cost of ownership for installers and end-users, creating stronger customer retention and premium pricing power. Tedlar's proven chemistry directly addresses these stakes: documented 20-year outdoor performance eliminates warranty risk, graffiti resistance solves vandalism complaints on transit/municipal projects, and extreme durability reduces replacement frequency—all of which strengthen Avery Dennison's competitive positioning in high-specification segments where current products underperform.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Avery Dennison just celebrated 90 years at ISA International Sign Expo 2025 (April 23-25) and exhibited at FESPA Middle East 2024, signaling active market positioning around heritage and innovation. The completion of the massive DPD fleet project (30,000 vehicles, 4,500 trailers over three years) demonstrates they're winning large-scale contracts but also reveals potential warranty exposure as those wraps approach their 5-12 year lifespan limits. With customer expectations rising for 15-20 year performance guarantees in architectural and municipal segments, NOW is the optimal time to engage [Name] about next-generation protective technologies that extend product life beyond current vinyl limitations. Additionally, the competitive pressure from 3M, HP, and specialty PVF manufacturers showcasing at the same trade shows creates urgency to evaluate differentiation strategies for upcoming product roadmap decisions and 2026 trade show messaging.

personalization_hooks.hook: Avery Dennison's current wrapping films max out at 12-year outdoor life, but municipal transit and architectural facade RFPs increasingly require 15-20 year performance warranties that exceed cast vinyl capabilities
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Open by acknowledging the gap between current product limits and emerging market specifications. Position Tedlar as the enabling technology that allows Avery Dennison to credibly bid on ultra-premium segments currently inaccessible—focus on the business opportunity rather than product specs.

personalization_hooks.hook: The 30,000-vehicle DPD fleet project represents both a success story and future warranty exposure as those wraps approach end-of-life, requiring costly replacement cycles
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Reference their flagship project as proof of market leadership, then pivot to how protective overlaminate technology could double the service life—transforming fleet economics and creating a competitive moat. Frame it as reducing customer churn from maintenance burden.

personalization_hooks.hook: Recent ISA and FESPA exhibitions position Avery Dennison's 90-year heritage, but 3M and specialty PVF manufacturers are aggressively marketing superior graffiti resistance and extreme-climate performance
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Start with respect for their market presence, then introduce Tedlar as a strategic response to competitive encroachment. Emphasize that co-development or licensing allows them to leapfrog competitors by combining their vinyl expertise with proven PVF chemistry—creating an unassailable premium tier.

recommended_approach: Lead with the innovation opportunity angle—frame Tedlar as a technology partnership that solves specific performance gaps preventing Avery Dennison from capturing ultra-premium architectural and transit segments. Avoid generic 'better durability' claims; instead, connect directly to their business reality: current products can't meet emerging 15-20 year warranty specifications, which locks them out of high-value municipal contracts. Position the conversation as exploratory—'Would it make sense to discuss how PVF protective layers could extend your Supreme Wrapping Film performance envelope for architectural and transit applications?' This respects their innovation evaluation process while making the business case concrete.
